land.text: the southern alluvium around Uruk, where the Uruk-period culture gives way to Cliopatria's first city-state row

predecessors.note: uruk-period (a culture dossier, another group) names this state as its successor and books the loss -3400; the core is handed over at 3400 BCE.

land.text: Sumer: 'In his conquest of Sumer circa 2300 BC, Sargon of Akkad' took Uruk, Ur and Umma and 'laid waste' the land from Lagash to the sea

successors.note: Sargon's defeat of Lugal-zage-si is dated 'around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292' on the Akkadian Empire page; the Akkadian state itself was founded c. 2334 at Akkad.

capitals.name: Uruk (Warka)
capitals.note: No single seat: Uruk is the leading city of the Uruk and Jemdet Nasr periods ('Uruk reached an impressive area of 250 hectares during the Uruk IV phase'); the Sumerian King List then places the kingship at Kish.

capitals.name: Kish (Tell al-Uhaymir)
capitals.note: 'After the flood had swept over, and the kingship had descended from heaven, the kingship was in Kish'; Enmebaragesi (r. c. 2750 BC) is 'the first name confirmed by archaeological finds'; Mesilim (r. c. 2550 BC) arbitrated between Lagash and Umma. A hegemony, not an administration. From -2500 to -2426 the collective has no seat of its own: Ur and Lagash led, and their dossiers (first-dynasty-of-ur, lagash) draw those capitals.

capitals.name: Uruk (Warka)
capitals.note: Lugal-kinishe-dudu (c. 2400 BC) 'King of Uruk and Ur'; Enshakushanna (c. 2350 BC) 'lord of Sumer and king of all the land'; Lugal-zage-si (r. c. 2340–2316 on the Uruk page, c. 2358–2334 on his own) 'established his new capital' at Uruk.

keyframe_review.note: 22,012 km2 around Uruk for -3400..-3201. 'The Uruk period provides the earliest signs of the existence of states in the Near East, a process of state formation, at least during the Late Uruk' (ca. 3500–3300/3200 BC); proto-cuneiform 'appears around 3400-3300'. No infobox area exists for a period; the Sumer page's population (0.8–1.5 million) is undated. Before -3400 the Uruk culture is a culture (rule 8), not this state.

35,615 km2 for -3200..-3001, the Uruk III / Jemdet Nasr stage ('Uruk III epigraphic stage, ca. 3200-3000 BC'). The colonies of the Uruk expansion (Habuba Kabira, Hacinebi, Susa II) are rightly not drawn: 'after 3300/3200 BC this dynamic ceased'.

45,290 km2 for -3000..-2701: 'Jemdet Nasr period: c. 3100 – c. 2900 BC', 'Early Dynastic I: c. 2900 – c. 2800 BC', 'Early Dynastic II: c. 2800 – c. 2600 BC'; the cities 'lie in the Euphrates-Tigris alluvial plain, south of Baghdad'. Growth is the spread of cities, not conquest (ledger, confidence 1).

80,618 km2 for -2700..-2501, Early Dynastic II–IIIa: 'Sumer was divided into about thirteen independent cities' separated by canals and boundary stones, and in the north Kish 'may have led a large territorial state'. The eastern tongue toward Susiana (bbox to 48.9 E, 64 cells of Khuzestan) rests only on Enmebaragesi's (c. 2750) and Eannatum's (c. 2450) Elamite victories, which the pages give as campaigns, not land; the Eannatum raid is a hatched occupation in lagash and elam. [fixer me-01: ok -> adjust, Khuzestan removed so that Susiana is Elam's alone.]

correction.text: Sumer and Akkad of the Early Dynastic city-states without the eastern tongue into Khuzestan: the History of Sumer page gives the Sumerian cities no Elamite land ('Eannatum's campaigns extended beyond the confines of Sumer, and he overran a part of Elam'; Enmebaragesi 'said to have defeated Elam'), and elam holds Susiana (elam_-2700: Khuzestan and Ilam)

Sumer and Akkad from Lagash and the sea to Kish and Akshak, without Mari and without Khuzestan: the Early Dynastic page lists Mari as a separate state ('centered on cities such as Kish, Mari, Nagar, and Ebla'), Eannatum only 'demanded tribute as far as Mari', and the History of Sumer page gives no Sumerian city Elamite land (elam holds Susiana)

keyframe_review.note: 106,576 km2 for -2500..-2301, the largest shape: its north-western arm reaches 40.5 E / 34.8 N, which is Mari's middle Euphrates. Mari was its own kingdom (dossier mari), tributary to Lagash c. 2450 and raided by Lugal-zage-si ('a successful raiding party'); removed. The years are right: the dissolve is -2300. [fixer me-01: Khuzestan removed as in -2700.] For -2500..-2426 the ledger hands the plain to first-dynasty-of-ur (-2500) and, through it, to lagash, and takes it back at -2425, so this shape is drawn in full before -2500 and from -2425; the city dossiers draw the hegemonies.

correction.text: a fragment around Ur and Eridu (8,294 km2) dated -2300..-2251: Sargon had conquered Sumer 'around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292' and this land is the Akkadian Empire's; draw nothing for the Sumerian city-states after -2300

keyframe_review.note: After Sargon 'defeated Lugal-zage-si, bringing Lower Mesopotamia under his control' there was no independent Sumerian state until the Gutian period; the Akkadian -2300 shape covers this ground.

correction.text: the Third Dynasty of Ur (c. 2112–2004), 'King of Sumer and Akkad', with a periphery 'from Urbilum to Pashime and Susa': Cliopatria's 12,568 km2 fragment at Ur and Eridu is that state's heartland and its 131,488 km2 'Gutian Dynasty' outline of the same years is its realm; reviewed in third-dynasty-of-ur. The shape and the years -2100..-2001 belong to third-dynasty-of-ur (-2112..-2004), which lies outside this state's life: the collective ended in -2300 (dissolve into akkadian-empire).

keyframe_review.note: Not the Sumerian city-states: in -2100..-2001 Sumer was one state under Ur (new dossier third-dynasty-of-ur, which uses the Gutian Dynasty -2100 shape).

correction.text: Sumer in the Isin-Larsa period ('c. 2004 – c. 1736 BC' on the Sumer page): the north (Isin, Nippur) is the kingdom of Isin, the south (Larsa, Ur, Lagash) the kingdom of Larsa after 'Gungunum captured the city of Ur'; divided between the dossiers isin and larsa

keyframe_review.note: Two states, not a collective: reviewed with corrections in isin and larsa.

correction.text: Rim-Sin I's Larsa (r. 1822–1763), which 'controlled about 10–15 other city-states' and took Isin c. 1792; it fell to Hammurabi after 'a six-month siege' c. 1763, two years before Cliopatria's -1761

keyframe_review.note: Reviewed in larsa; Isin keeps its own shape to -1792 (dossier isin).

region.text: the Late Uruk cities of the lower Euphrates around Uruk

ledger.note: 3400 BCE: the first city-states form around Uruk. 'The Uruk period provides the earliest signs of the existence of states in the Near East, a process of state formation, at least during the Late Uruk' (ca. 3500–3300/3200 BC); proto-cuneiform 'appears around 3400-3300, essentially for administrative purposes'. The year is Cliopatria's rounding of the Late Uruk phase. Handed over from the uruk-period culture dossier (its /ledger/3, loss of Babylonia, counterpart this dossier).

region.text: the Jemdet Nasr (Uruk III) spread of settlement

ledger.note: 3200 BCE: the cities multiply in the Jemdet Nasr stage. The page dates the 'Uruk III epigraphic stage, ca. 3200-3000 BC' but describes no territorial growth; the event only explains Cliopatria's larger shape.
3000 BCE: Early Dynastic I. 'Jemdet Nasr period: c. 3100 – c. 2900 BC', 'Early Dynastic I: c. 2900 – c. 2800 BC'; growth of settlement, no conquest on the page.

2750 BCE: the kingship is at Kish. 'After the flood had swept over, and the kingship had descended from heaven, the kingship was in Kish'; Enmebaragesi (r. c. 2750 BC) 'is the first name confirmed by archaeological finds from his reign'; the History of Sumer page has him defeat Elam and build Enlil's temple at Nippur.

region.text: the north around Kish and the Tigris side

ledger.note: 2700 BCE: 'about thirteen independent cities' of Early Dynastic II–III. The page describes the cities and Kish's 'large territorial state', not a frontier.

region.text: Lagash, Girsu and Nina, the land of Ur-Nanshe's new kingdom

ledger.note: 2520 BCE: Lagash becomes a kingdom of its own under Ur-Nanshe ('r. c. 2520 BC'). Mirror of lagash /ledger/0 (found), whose note carries the page quotes; the collective's K3 and K4 shapes still contain this ground, which the lagash dossier draws from its own keyframes (decision of the me-01 fixer: the city dossiers are booked against the collective as splits, losses, occupations and dissolves, and the cities are drawn over it).

region.text: the Sumerian plain under Ur's lead, without the cities Lagash and Umma, which keep their own dossiers

ledger.note: 2500 BCE: the hegemony passes to Ur. Mesannepada ('Mesannepada: r. c. 2500 BC (80 years)'), 'King of Kish', whose dynasty 'apparently led a union of south Mesopotamian polities'; 'Then Uruk was defeated and the kingship was taken to Ur'. Booked as the plain passing to Ur for -2500..-2451, mirror of first-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/1; Lagash and Umma keep their own cities. Replaces the capital move to Ur of the first version.

region.text: 'all of Sumer, including Ur, Nippur, Akshak (controlled by Zuzu), Larsa, and Uruk' as Eannatum's domain, with Umma (tributary) and Ur kept as their own cities

ledger.note: 2425 BCE: Eannatum's hegemony lapses and the plain returns to the collective, now led from Uruk. Enannatum I 'r. c. 2425 BC (MC)' succeeds; Kish 'regained its independence after his death' (Eannatum page). Lugal-kinishe-dudu (fl. c. 2400 BC) 'was a King and (ensi) of Uruk and Ur'. Mirror of lagash /ledger/6; year bridged to the successor's accession. Replaces the capital moves to Lagash (-2450) and back to Uruk (-2425) of the first version.

2400 BCE: Uruk holds Ur. Lugal-kinishe-dudu (fl. c. 2400 BC) 'was a King and (ensi) of Uruk and Ur' and 'proclaimed himself king of Ur and Kish'. Hatched, from the occupier's side; first-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/3 is the owner's. Entemena of Lagash and he 'established brotherhood' (his inscription), so Lagash was an ally, not a subject.

region.text: Kish, seized by Enshakushanna of Uruk

ledger.note: 2350 BCE: Uruk seizes Kish. Enshakushanna 'seized Kish and imprisoned its king Embi-Ishtar around 2350 B.C.' (the page, as quoted in kish /ledger/4); 'lord of Sumer and king of all the land' (Uruk page). Hatched, from the occupier's side; kish /ledger/4 is the owner's.
2340 BCE: the hold on Ur becomes Lugal-zage-si's annexation; Ur ends as a state (the gain two events below). Mirror of first-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/4.
2340 BCE: the hold on Kish becomes annexation ('invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa', Lugal-zage-si page). Mirror of kish /ledger/5.
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si 'annexed most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina'. Mirror of lagash /ledger/11 (dissolve).
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si 'invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa'. Mirror of kish /ledger/6 (dissolve); Sargon, Ur-Zababa's cup-bearer, founds Akkad on this ground (akkadian-empire).
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si 'took Uruk and Ur, and made Uruk his capital' (History of Sumer page, as quoted in first-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/5). Mirror of that dissolve.

2340 BCE: Umma's ensi Lugal-zage-si 'established his new capital' at Uruk and Umma becomes a city of the collective's last kingdom. Mirror of umma /ledger/3 (dissolve). The Ur and Uruk he held from Umma are booked here (occupation of Ur, rename), not in umma.

2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si of Umma unites Sumer from Uruk. He 'began his career as énsi of Umma', 'annexed most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina', 'invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa, Ur, Nippur, and Larsa' and 'established his new capital' at Uruk, claiming 'all the lands between the upper and the lower seas'. His page gives r. c. 2358–2334, the Uruk page c. 2340–2316, the Umma page a zenith c. 2350; -2340 follows the Uruk and Umma pages. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Lower Mesopotamia: Uruk, whose walls Sargon 'tore down', Ur, Lagash 'to the sea', Umma

ledger.note: 2300 BCE: Sargon of Akkad conquers Sumer. He 'defeated Lugal-zage-si, bringing Lower Mesopotamia under his control', 'around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292'; the Lagash page: 'In his conquest of Sumer circa 2300 BC'. Sargon's reign began c. 2334, so the Akkadian dossier starts at Akkad in -2334 and takes Sumer here.

wars.name: Lagash–Umma border conflict

zones.text: 'the Guʾedena, a fertile area lying between them' (Lagash and Umma)

wars.outcome: Eannatum defeated Ush of Umma (Stele of the Vultures, c. 2450), made Umma tributary and fixed the border with Enakalle; Ur-Lumma and Il of Umma fought Entemena, who 'reported' the conflict c. 2400. An internal war of the collective; the cities' own dossiers carry it.
wars.note: Mesilim of Kish (c. 2550 on the Kish page, c. 2500 on the Early Dynastic page) had arbitrated an earlier round. Gu-edena is not in the gazetteer.

wars.name: Eannatum's campaigns
wars.outcome: Lagash 'conquered all of Sumer', overran parts of Elam and took tribute from Mari; the conquests lapsed at Eannatum's death (Kish 'regained its independence after his death').

wars.name: Lugal-zage-si's conquest of Sumer
wars.outcome: Umma's ensi took Lagash, Uruk, Ur, Kish, Nippur and Larsa and ruled Sumer from Uruk; no outer border moved (the raid to the 'upper sea' held no land, 'a successful raiding party').

wars.name: Sargon's conquest of Sumer
wars.outcome: Sargon 'defeated the city of Uruk and tore down its walls', 'was victorious over Ur in battle, conquered the city and destroyed its wall', led Lugal-zage-si 'in a neck-stock to Enlil's temple in Nippur' and annexed Sumer.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line anywhere: the cities were 'separated by canals and boundary stones' (Early Dynastic page), and the outer edge toward the steppe, the Zagros and the Gulf (whose coast then 'nearly reached Ur') is approximate. The Lagash–Umma boundary stele (Mesilim, Eannatum) is the one dated line and is local.

notes:
SPLIT: Cliopatria's one row 'Sumerian City-States' (-3400..-1761) is at least four states. This dossier keeps the collective of city-states from the Late Uruk state formation (-3400) to Sargon's conquest (-2300), with the Kish hegemony as a capital move and Lugal-zage-si's kingdom as one rename (the Ur, Lagash and Uruk hegemonies are booked against the city dossiers, see OVERLAP). The later shapes go to new dossiers: third-dynasty-of-ur (-2112..-2004; it also uses Cliopatria's mislabelled 'Gutian Dynasty' -2100 outline), isin (-2018..-1792) and larsa (-2025..-1763); the -2300..-2251 fragment is Akkadian land and is marked wrong. All nine shapes are reviewed here so the validator sees them; the split dossiers review their own again with corrections, and the verdicts agree.

OVERLAP, settled by the me-01 fixer (the reviewer asked for a decision): the city dossiers written in this batch (lagash -2520..-2340, second-dynasty-of-lagash -2164..-2110, kish -2900..-2340, first-dynasty-of-ur -2600..-2340, umma -2500..-2340, uruk -2154..-2112, plus ebla and mari) are drawn over the collective, and every event that moves land between them and the collective is booked on both sides: split of Lagash (-2520), the plain to Ur (-2500, loss) and back from Lagash (-2425, gain), the Uruk hold on Ur (-2400..-2340) and Kish (-2350..-2340) as hatched occupations, and the dissolves of lagash, kish, first-dynasty-of-ur and umma into the collective in -2340 as four gains. The hegemonies are therefore no longer capital moves here (the Ur, Lagash and second Uruk seats are removed from identity.capitals; -2500..-2426 has no seat of its own). Eannatum's Susa occupation and Mari tribute (formerly /ledger/7-10 here) are lagash's alone. Umma's holding of Ur and Uruk under Lugal-zage-si is booked here (the occupation of Ur and the -2340 rename), not as a gain in umma. Not done: the K3/K4 shapes still contain the city areas for the whole of -2700..-2301; the compiler should draw the city dossiers over them for their years. Alternative if the orchestrator prefers: demote this dossier to the background of the Early Dynastic period and re-point the cities' counterparts to nobody.

CHRONOLOGY: all dates middle chronology as the Wikipedia infoboxes give them (Sargon 2334–2279). The pages disagree on Lugal-zage-si (2358–2334 on his page, 2340–2316 on Uruk's, zenith c. 2350 on Umma's) and on the conquest of Sumer ('around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292' versus the infobox's 2334 for the empire). The Sumer page's short-chronology dates (Sargon's conquest 'around 2270 BC') were not used.

GAZETTEER: Gu-edena (region, between Girsu and Umma) is not in the gazetteer. The area growth -3200/-3000/-2700 is settlement, recorded as gains from nobody at confidence 1 because no page describes a frontier.

PREDECESSOR (me-01 fixer): uruk-period (another group) books the loss -3400 to this state and names it as its successor; the found event now carries counterpart uruk-period. History of Sumer page, re-read for the fixer: it gives Sumerian cities no Elamite land (Khuzestan removed from the -2700 and -2500 shapes); Lugal-Ane-mundu of Adab, who 'ruled from the Persian Gulf to the Mediterranean, and up to the Zagros Mountains, including Elam' (undated), is a claim, and Adab has no dossier.

THIN ITEM (growth -3200/-3000/-2700): the Jemdet Nasr period page, opened for this fix, says only that its 'geographical distribution is limited to south-central Iraq' (c. 3100–2900 BC, pottery found from Ur to Abu Salabikh and, painted, in the Hamrin Mountains); it gives no extent, no state and no frontier, so the gains from nobody stay at confidence 1.
